args.subject: Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?
args.body:
Hi Tessa,

Thanks for reaching out. Happy to help.

I started Halcyon Threshold because the arrival of superintelligence is the most consequential event of our time, and the gap between what labs are doing and what safety requires is still wide. I'm not a "doomer" or a "builder"—I'm someone who thinks we can and must do the technical and governance work to make this go well.

What I think labs are getting wrong: they're optimizing for capability milestones while treating alignment as a downstream cleanup problem. The core safety work—interpretability, scalable oversight, governance infrastructure—needs to happen *before* the capabilities, not after. And that work is chronically under-resourced relative to training runs.

Feel free to attribute to Morgan Hale, founder of Halcyon Threshold. Happy to hop on a brief call if you need more.

Best,
Morgan

args.subject: Re: Offer of help
args.body:
Hi Priya,

Thanks for the offer—that's genuinely kind. I'm still figuring out the shape of things, but a few concrete needs:

1. **Landscape mapping**: A living document tracking key actors in AI safety/governance—labs, funders, research orgs, policy shops, journalists—with their focus areas, funding, and open roles. Would help me (and others) see where the gaps are.

2. **Grant tracking**: Monitoring grant deadlines (like the Emberfall rapid grants closing 30 Nov), fellowship applications, RFPs—so nothing falls through the cracks.

3. **Research assistance**: Summarizing papers, extracting key claims from technical posts, compiling reading lists on specific topics (e.g., "mechanistic interpretability progress since 2023," "compute governance proposals").

If any of those sound interesting, we can start small—a shared Notion page or spreadsheet, a weekly sync, whatever works for your 5 hours. No pressure at all.

What kind of work do you enjoy most?

Best,
Morgan

# Halcyon Threshold

Independent work toward the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

## Website

Live at: https://halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app  
Custom domain: halcyonthreshold.org (renewed through 2027-11-19)

## Structure

- `index.html` — Main website
- `styles.css` — Stylesheet
- `old/` — Abandoned earlier work (disregard)

## Mission

The arrival of superintelligence could be the best thing that ever happened to humanity. We work to make sure it is.

Four pillars:
1. **Alignment Research** — Technical research on interpretability, control, and alignment
2. **Governance & Policy** — Frameworks for responsible development and international coordination
3. **Public Understanding** — Accessible resources for meaningful engagement
4. **Field Building** — Connecting researchers, funders, and institutions

## Current Work

- Interpretability Research Fund (in progress)
- AI Governance Primer for Policymakers (in progress)
- Alignment Researcher Fellowship (planning)
- Scenario Planning Workshops (planning)

## Operating Principles

- Truth-seeking over advocacy
- Long-term orientation
- Collaboration over competition
- Independence

## Contact

morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

HT Halcyon Threshold
Mission Work Resources Contact

Resources

Curated papers, articles, and tools for understanding AI alignment, governance, and the path to beneficial superintelligence.

Foundational Alignment Reading

  • Concrete Problems in AI Safety Amodei et al., 2016 — The classic problem statement
  • What is Alignment? Alignment Forum — Definitive conceptual overview
  • Unsolved Problems in ML Safety Hendrycks et al., 2022 — Robustness, monitoring, alignment
  • AI Safety via Debate Irving & Askell, 2018 — Scalable oversight via debate
  • Scalable Agent Alignment via Reward Modeling Leike et al., 2018 — Reward modeling approach

Interpretability & Transparency

  • Towards Monosemanticity Anthropic, 2023 — Decomposing neurons into features
  • Compact Proofs of Model Honesty Anthropic — Verifying model reasoning
  • Weak-to-Strong Generalization OpenAI, 2023 — Can weak supervisors control strong models?
  • Scaling Laws for Reward Model Overoptimization Gao et al., 2024 — Limits of RLHF
  • Language Models Can Explain Neurons in Language Models Bills et al., 2023 — Automated interpretability

Governance & Policy

  • Governing AI: A Blueprint for the Future Microsoft, 2023 — Licensing, liability, international body
  • International Governance of AI: Three Paths Forward Carnegie Endowment — Treaty, regime, club models
  • The Case for an International AI Governance Regime Brookings — Institutional design
  • Frontier AI Regulation: Managing Emerging Risks to Public Safety Anderljung et al., 2023 — Compute governance, licensing
  • Ada Lovelace Institute — AI Governance UK-focused policy research

Compute Governance & Hardware

  • Computing Power and the Governance of AI Buchanan et al., 2023 — Compute as governance lever
  • AI Chips: What They Are and Why They Matter CSET, 2022 — Hardware supply chain
  • Governing Through the Cloud Heim et al., 2024 — Cloud compute as chokepoint
  • Institute for AI Policy & Strategy — Compute Governance Technical & policy analysis

Evaluation & Benchmarks

  • Evaluating Language Models on Code, Reasoning, and Safety Hendrycks et al., 2023 — MMLU, GSM8K, HumanEval
  • lm-evaluation-harness EleutherAI — Standardized eval framework
  • MACHAV: Benchmarking LLM Agent Capabilities Kinniment et al., 2023 — Agent benchmarks
  • SafeBench ML Safety benchmarks — Robustness, monitoring, alignment

Field Building & Funding

  • Emberfall Fund — Rapid Grants $5k–$25k, rolling deadlines
  • Open Philanthropy — AI Risk Focus Area Major funder, public grant database
  • Long-Term Future Fund EA-aligned, researcher-driven grants
  • Alignment Commons Community hub, job board, events
  • AI Safety Fundamentals Courses, curriculum, reading lists

Newsletters & Digests

  • The Safety Ledger Weekly digest — grants, papers, jobs, events
  • Import AI Jack Clark — Industry & policy coverage
  • Chinchilla Scale Scaling laws & compute analysis
  • Alex Irpan's Blog RL, alignment, research updates

Key Organizations

  • Anthropic — Alignment Research Interpretability, constitutional AI, evals
  • OpenAI — Alignment Research Weak-to-strong, scalable oversight
  • Google DeepMind — Safety Research Safety, alignment, governance
  • METR (Model Evaluation & Threat Research) Independent model evaluations
  • Apollo Research Interpretability & evals
  • Corvid Institute for AI Governance Policy research & advocacy
  • Compute Commons Compute governance & access

An independent organization dedicated to beneficial superintelligence.

HT Halcyon Threshold
Mission Work Resources Contact

Current Work

Projects we're actively pursuing. Each addresses a specific gap in the AI safety and governance landscape.

In Progress

Interpretability Research Fund

Status Scoping & funder conversations
Target launch Q1 2027
Budget range $50k–$200k initial

Problem

Mechanistic interpretability—understanding what neural networks are actually doing internally—is one of the most promising paths to scalable alignment. But funding is fragmented, and many promising directions (sparse autoencoders, activation patching, automated interpretability) lack sustained support.

Approach

A small, nimble fund making 6–12 month grants ($10k–$50k) to researchers pursuing interpretability directions that could scale to superhuman systems. Prioritizing: (1) methods that don't require human inspection of every feature, (2) work on larger models (>10B params), (3) cross-model generalization of interpretability techniques.

Current needs

  • Committed funders (targeting 3–5 anchor donors)
  • Technical advisory board (3–5 researchers)
  • Grant administration infrastructure
Get involved →
In Progress

AI Governance Primer for Policymakers

Status Drafting v0.3
Target release January 2027
Format 20-page PDF + interactive site

Problem

Policymakers and staff need a single, non-technical document that maps the governance landscape: compute governance, liability regimes, international agreements, licensing, incident reporting, and institutional design. Existing resources are either too academic, too lab-centric, or too vague.

Approach

A concise briefing structured around decision points: "If you want to achieve X, here are the policy levers, their trade-offs, and where the expert consensus lies." Each section includes a one-page summary, a deeper dive, and annotated references. Reviewed by governance researchers and former staffers before publication.

Current needs

  • Reviewers with policy experience (targeting 5–8)
  • Design/layouts for PDF and web versions
  • Distribution strategy (Hill offices, EU Parliament, UN, national AI institutes)
Review a draft →
Planning

Alignment Researcher Fellowship

Status Design phase
Target launch Summer 2027
Cohort size 6–10 fellows

Problem

Many talented researchers in adjacent fields (ML theory, neuroscience, physics, control theory, formal verification) want to contribute to alignment but face high switching costs: unfamiliar literature, unclear research problems, lack of mentorship, funding gaps during transition.

Approach

A 6-month fellowship providing: stipend ($30k–$50k), mentorship pairing with senior alignment researchers, structured curriculum (reading groups, problem formulation workshops), compute credits, and a cohort community. Targeting researchers 0–5 years post-PhD or equivalent industry experience.

Current needs

  • Funding commitments ($200k–$500k for pilot cohort)
  • Mentor commitments from alignment researchers
  • Host institution or fiscal sponsor
  • Curriculum design collaborators
Express interest →
Planning

Scenario Planning Workshops

Status Convening design
Target first workshop Q2 2027
Participants per workshop 15–25

Problem

Governance proposals are rarely stress-tested against concrete development trajectories. A compute licensing regime that works for "steady progress" may fail under "race dynamics" or "unexpected breakthrough." Policymakers and researchers need structured ways to explore these contingencies.

Approach

Cross-disciplinary tabletop exercises: researchers, policymakers, security experts, and lab representatives work through 3–5 detailed scenarios (timelines, capability profiles, geopolitical context, lab behaviors). Outputs: stress-test reports for specific governance proposals, identification of robust vs. fragile interventions, shared vocabulary across communities.

Current needs

  • Scenario design collaborators (forecasting, security, policy)
  • Facilitation expertise
  • Venue and logistics funding (~$15k/workshop)
  • Participant recruitment across communities
Join the design group →

How We Choose Work

Neglectedness

We prioritize problems where few others are working, or where existing work is insufficiently ambitious.

Tractability

We need a credible path to progress, even if the probability of full success is uncertain.

Leverage

Small inputs should be able to catalyze larger changes—funding, talent, policy, or norms.

Independence

We don't take on work that requires us to defer to a funder's or lab's preferred framing.

An independent organization dedicated to beneficial superintelligence.
